claims.text: The conventional elemental Cr coating on zirconium-alloy cladding is prone to interdiffusion-induced premature failure at elevated temperatures.
A 50–100 nm amorphous Al2O3 interlayer deposited by ALD is the proposed intervention between the zirconium-alloy substrate and Cr coating.
The Al2O3 interlayer will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion will delay or prevent premature Cr-coating failure.
The Al2O3-modified coating will maintain adequate protection during normal subcritical-water operation.
The Al2O3-modified coating will maintain adequate protection during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
A continuous Al2O3 interlayer acts as a physical and chemical diffusion barrier between Cr and the Zr-alloy substrate.
The Al2O3 interlayer blocks diffusion pathways and prevents direct Cr–Zr atomic intermixing.
Suppressing Cr–Zr intermixing inhibits the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
Inhibiting deleterious intermetallic phases preserves coating adhesion and structural integrity.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated Zr alloy, the Al2O3-modified system will show significantly delayed or suppressed Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the baseline, the Al2O3-modified system will have enhanced coating durability.
Relative to the baseline, the Al2O3-modified system will maintain oxidation protection in both reactor-operation and accident conditions.
The proposed normal-operation boundary is subcritical water at approximately 300°C for up to about 10,000 hours.
The proposed accident boundary is steam at approximately 1100°C for about 1 hour.
The long-term stability of the Al2O3 barrier under reactor-relevant radiation and thermal cycling is unresolved.
